Let \(k\) be the number of digits of \(r\). Then the concatenated number is  
\[
N=q\cdot 10^k+r,
\]
and we have
\[
p^2=N+3=q\cdot 10^k+r+3.
\]

Since \(10^k\) is even, \(q\cdot 10^k\) is even. If \(r\) were odd, then \(N\) would be odd, so \(p^2=N+3\) would be even. This forces \(p=2\), giving \(p^2=4\), hence \(N=1\), impossible. Therefore \(r\) must be the only even prime:
\[
r=2.
\]
Since \(2\) has one digit, \(k=1\). Thus
\[
p^2=10q+2+3=10q+5=5(2q+1).
\]
So \(5\mid p^2\), and since \(p\) is prime, \(p=5\). Then \(25=10q+5\), so \(q=2\), which is prime.

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
